prompts.title: Postgres vs Mongo for billing
prompts.text: A 12-person engineering team is choosing a primary datastore for a new multi-tenant subscription billing system that must support proration, refunds, dunning retries, and monthly invoice generation across roughly 40,000 tenants. Two finalists remain: PostgreSQL (relational, with JSONB columns available for flexible fields) and MongoDB (document store, with multi-document transactions available since v4.0). Evaluate the two options against these four criteria: (1) correctness guarantees for money-related writes under concurrent updates, (2) ease of evolving the invoice line-item schema as pricing plans change quarterly, (3) the team's ability to write ad-hoc financial reports for finance stakeholders, and (4) operational maturity of backup/restore and point-in-time recovery tooling. For each criterion, give a short assessment of both databases, then end with a single unambiguous recommendation - do not conclude with 'it depends'. Justify the recommendation in 3-4 sentences referencing the specific requirements of a billing system.

prompts.title: Cache stampede postmortem
prompts.text:
Write an incident postmortem based on the log excerpt below from a checkout-service on-call rotation. Include sections for Summary, Timeline, Root Cause, Impact, and Action Items (at least 4, each with an owner placeholder and priority). The postmortem must end with a clear severity rating (SEV1/SEV2/SEV3) and a one-sentence verdict on whether the on-call response was adequate.

Log excerpt (all times UTC):
14:02:11 cache-node-3 WARN key 'product_catalog:v2' TTL expired, eviction scheduled
14:02:12 cache-node-3 INFO eviction complete, 1 key removed
14:02:13 api-gateway INFO request rate 340 req/s (baseline 310 req/s)
14:02:14 checkout-svc ERROR cache miss for 'product_catalog:v2', falling through to DB
14:02:14 checkout-svc ERROR cache miss for 'product_catalog:v2', falling through to DB
14:02:14 checkout-svc ERROR cache miss for 'product_catalog:v2', falling through to DB
(...repeated 8,412 times across 14:02:14-14:02:47)
postgres-primary WARN connection pool exhausted, 200/200 connections in use
14:02:51 api-gateway ERROR upstream timeout checkout-svc, 504 returned to client
14:03:05 api-gateway ERROR error rate 61% over last 30s
14:03:40 oncall-bot PAGE triggered: checkout-svc error budget burn rate 14.2x
14:06:12 engineer-jhall ACK page, begins investigation
14:11:30 engineer-jhall INFO identified missing lock around cache repopulation on miss
14:12:00 engineer-jhall INFO manually re-warmed 'product_catalog:v2' key
14:12:40 checkout-svc INFO cache hit rate recovering, now 94%
14:15:00 api-gateway INFO error rate back to baseline 0.3%

Assume the cache repopulation code had no mutex or single-flight guard, so every concurrent miss issued its own database query.

prompts.title: Kubernetes vs Nomad rollout
prompts.text: A platform team of 6 engineers currently runs 50 nodes across two data centers and is deciding between Kubernetes and HashiCorp Nomad as the long-term orchestration layer, with a hard requirement to support both containerized services and a legacy fleet of non-containerized batch jobs. Assess Kubernetes and Nomad against these criteria: operational complexity for a small team, richness of the ecosystem for observability and service mesh integration, native support for mixed container/non-container workloads, and multi-cloud portability if the company later needs to run in a second cloud provider. Weigh the criteria explicitly - state which criterion matters most for a 6-person team - and finish with a definitive recommendation of one system, not a hedge. Include one specific risk the losing option would have introduced if chosen instead.

prompts.title: Duplicate webhook processing incident
prompts.text:
Below is a trimmed log from a payment-processing worker that consumes Stripe webhook events from a queue. Analyze it and produce a postmortem with headings Summary, Root Cause, Blast Radius, and Remediation (short-term fix plus long-term fix), ending with a one-line verdict stating whether customers were financially impacted and whether a customer-facing apology is warranted.

09:14:02 worker-1 INFO received event evt_9f2a charge.succeeded order=ORD-88123
09:14:02 worker-2 INFO received event evt_9f2a charge.succeeded order=ORD-88123
09:14:03 worker-1 INFO marking ORD-88123 as paid, incrementing loyalty_points +150
09:14:03 worker-2 INFO marking ORD-88123 as paid, incrementing loyalty_points +150
09:14:03 worker-1 INFO dispatching fulfillment email for ORD-88123
09:14:03 worker-2 INFO dispatching fulfillment email for ORD-88123
09:14:04 notification-svc INFO sent 2 fulfillment emails for ORD-88123 within 900ms
09:41:17 support-bot INFO ticket #55210 opened: 'why did I get two order confirmation emails and double loyalty points?'
10:02:00 engineer-r.diaz INFO queue consumer has no idempotency key check on event.id before processing
10:03:11 engineer-r.diaz INFO confirms webhook retried by Stripe after a 4-second ack timeout on worker-1, both workers pulled the same event because the queue's visibility timeout was shorter than processing time
10:04:00 engineer-r.diaz INFO audit shows 37 orders affected over the past 9 days with double loyalty_points credit, 0 orders double-charged since payment capture itself was idempotent at Stripe's end

prompts.title: Monorepo tradeoff for startup
prompts.text: A 12-engineer startup building three products (a web app, a mobile app, and a shared backend API) is debating whether to consolidate three existing separate git repositories into a single monorepo. Evaluate the tradeoff along these axes: build/CI time as the codebase grows, ease of atomic cross-project changes, onboarding friction for new hires, and tooling maturity (given the team currently uses plain npm workspaces, not Bazel or Nx). Give a concrete recommendation for whether this specific team should migrate now, migrate later, or not at all, and justify it with reference to their team size and the fact they ship weekly. Do not simply list pros and cons - commit to an answer.

prompts.title: gRPC vs REST internally
prompts.text: An internal platform exposes about 30 microservices that currently talk to each other over JSON REST with hand-maintained OpenAPI specs. The team is considering migrating internal (not public-facing) service-to-service calls to gRPC. Compare gRPC and REST/JSON specifically for internal use across these criteria: p99 latency overhead for small payloads (under 2KB), the cost of enforcing contract compatibility as 30 services evolve independently, developer experience for debugging a failing call with curl-like tools, and the learning curve for engineers who have only worked with REST. State a final verdict on whether this specific migration is worth it given the team has no protobuf experience today, and note one concrete condition under which your verdict would flip.

prompts.title: DNS misconfiguration outage review
prompts.text:
Produce a postmortem from the log excerpt below covering a regional outage caused by a DNS record change. Structure it as Summary, Detection Timeline, Root Cause, Customer Impact (estimate affected request volume from the numbers given), and three concrete prevention measures. Close with a verdict on whether the change should have required peer review before deployment.

03:11:00 deploy-bot INFO terraform apply started by user 'automation-ci', change set includes dns_record.api_eu_west
03:11:04 deploy-bot INFO terraform apply complete, api-eu.example.com CNAME updated from lb-eu-old.example.com to lb-eu-new.example.com
03:11:40 monitoring INFO synthetic check api-eu.example.com latency 890ms (baseline 45ms)
03:12:15 monitoring WARN synthetic check api-eu.example.com failing, DNS resolution returning NXDOMAIN intermittently
03:12:15 support-queue INFO 4 new tickets in last 60s referencing 'cannot reach app'
03:14:00 monitoring ERROR synthetic check api-eu.example.com 100% failure rate
03:14:30 support-queue INFO ticket volume now 61 in last 3 minutes, mostly EU customers
03:16:00 oncall-page PAGE triggered: eu-west availability below 50%
03:19:44 engineer-k.omondi ACK, discovers lb-eu-new.example.com was not yet provisioned, only lb-eu-old existed
03:21:00 engineer-k.omondi INFO reverting CNAME to lb-eu-old.example.com
03:23:10 monitoring INFO synthetic check recovering, latency 52ms
03:26:00 engineer-k.omondi INFO full recovery confirmed, DNS TTL was 300s so propagation delay explains the tail of the incident

Assume EU-west normally serves about 18% of global traffic and the region was fully unreachable for roughly 15 minutes.

prompts.title: Sync vs event-driven fulfillment
prompts.text: An e-commerce order fulfillment system currently makes synchronous calls from the order service to inventory, payment, and shipping-label services in sequence, and is considering a move to an event-driven architecture using a message broker instead. Evaluate this architectural change against: failure isolation when one downstream service is degraded, the operational cost of debugging a multi-step business process that no longer has a single call stack, latency for the customer-facing 'place order' request, and the team's current lack of any existing message broker in production. Give a definitive verdict on whether the migration is worth doing now versus deferring it, and specify what triggering condition (e.g., a scale threshold or a specific recurring failure mode) would change your answer.

prompts.title: Terraform vs Pulumi migration
prompts.text: Two years into using hand-written Terraform HCL across roughly 200 files, a platform team is evaluating a switch to Pulumi, which lets them write infrastructure code in TypeScript instead. Compare the two on: state management maturity and drift-detection tooling, the ergonomics of expressing conditional logic and loops (HCL's limited expressiveness versus a general-purpose language), the risk and cost of migrating 200 existing files, and hiring/onboarding given most infra engineers already know Terraform. Provide one clear recommendation - stay, migrate fully, or adopt a hybrid approach for new modules only - and defend the choice against the specific migration cost mentioned.

prompts.title: Node.js heap leak diagnosis
prompts.text:
Analyze the log/metrics excerpt below from a Node.js order-processing service and write a postmortem-style analysis covering Root Cause, Why It Took 6 Hours To Notice, and a verdict on whether the fix (restarting pods every 4 hours as a stopgap) is an acceptable long-term mitigation or must be replaced with a real fix.

[metrics] 08:00 heap_used=180MB rss=310MB active_handles=42
[metrics] 10:00 heap_used=410MB rss=540MB active_handles=890
[metrics] 12:00 heap_used=780MB rss=920MB active_handles=2140
[metrics] 13:30 heap_used=1180MB rss=1340MB active_handles=3980
[log] 13:41 GC pause 340ms (previously averaging 12ms)
[log] 13:52 GC pause 1120ms
[log] 14:03 process OOM-killed, restarted by orchestrator
[log] 14:03 engineer note: heap snapshot taken just before OOM shows 3,981 retained EventEmitter listener objects all referencing closed database connections from a connection-pool 'on error' handler that was never removed
[log] 14:20 engineer note: the pool's error handler is re-registered on every request instead of once at startup, and the old handlers are never detached because the request-scoped connection object stays referenced by the closure

Assume this service handles roughly 40 requests per second at peak.

prompts.title: Build vs buy feature flags
prompts.text: A company with 25 engineers currently has no feature-flagging system and is deciding whether to buy a hosted feature-flag SaaS product or build a minimal in-house flag service backed by their existing Postgres database and Redis cache. Compare the two paths on: time to first flag in production, ongoing maintenance burden on the platform team, cost at their current scale (roughly 2 million flag evaluations per day) versus projected cost at 10x that scale, and the risk of vendor lock-in for a capability that touches every service. Give a firm recommendation for this specific company and identify the one scale threshold at which your recommendation would reverse.

prompts.title: Kafka vs RabbitMQ for events
prompts.text: An events pipeline needs to carry order-lifecycle events (created, paid, shipped, cancelled) to roughly 8 downstream consumers, some of which need to replay the last 7 days of events for backfills. Compare Kafka and RabbitMQ for this specific pipeline on: native support for long-retention replay, guarantees around per-key ordering, the operational burden of running either system with a 3-person infra team, and throughput headroom if order volume grows 5x. Conclude with an unambiguous choice of one system for this pipeline, explicitly addressing the replay requirement, since that is the requirement most likely to be decisive here.

prompts.title: Redis eviction storm postmortem
prompts.text:
A session-store outage last night traced back to Redis eviction; here is the log. Write a postmortem using headings Summary, Root Cause, Contributing Factors, and Action Items, and end with a verdict on whether the root cause was a capacity-planning failure or a code-level bug (or both), stating which one deserves the higher-priority fix.

21:00 redis-primary INFO used_memory 3.8GB of maxmemory 4GB
21:15 redis-primary INFO used_memory 3.95GB, evicted_keys counter begins incrementing
21:16 auth-svc WARN session lookup miss for token a91f..., forcing re-login
21:16 auth-svc WARN session lookup miss for token c223..., forcing re-login
21:17 auth-svc WARN 1,204 session lookup misses in last 60s (baseline near 0)
21:18 support-queue INFO surge of tickets: 'I keep getting logged out'
21:20 engineer-t.nakamura INFO checks redis INFO, maxmemory-policy is set to allkeys-lru, meaning any key including active sessions can be evicted, not just expired ones
21:22 engineer-t.nakamura INFO discovers a batch analytics job introduced last week writes 2.1GB of temporary aggregation keys into the same Redis instance with no TTL and no separate namespace
21:35 engineer-t.nakamura INFO manually flushes the analytics keys, used_memory drops to 1.7GB, eviction stops, session miss rate returns to baseline within 4 minutes

prompts.title: TypeScript vs Python for ETL
prompts.text: A 4-person data platform team is building a new ETL pipeline that will grow from 15 to an expected 80 transformation jobs over the next year, and must choose between TypeScript (with strict mode) and Python (with type hints but no enforced strict mode) as the primary language. Evaluate on: the value of compile-time type checking as job count and contributor count grow, the maturity and breadth of each language's data/ETL ecosystem, ramp-up time for the team's current skill set (all four engineers are stronger in Python today), and long-term maintenance cost as jobs accumulate. Give a definitive recommendation, explicitly stating whether the team's current skill gap should outweigh the type-safety argument, and justify why.

prompts.title: Row-level security vs app checks
prompts.text: A multi-tenant SaaS application currently enforces tenant data isolation entirely in application code via a WHERE tenant_id = ? clause added to every query, and the team is considering moving that guarantee into the database using Postgres row-level security (RLS) policies instead. Compare the two approaches on: the blast radius of a single missed WHERE clause in application code versus a misconfigured RLS policy, query performance overhead RLS policies typically introduce, the ease of writing and testing raw analytical queries against the database directly, and how each approach affects a future migration to a different ORM. End with a clear verdict on which approach this team should adopt as its primary isolation guarantee, while application-layer checks may still remain as defense in depth - state explicitly whether defense in depth is worth the double maintenance cost here.

prompts.title: Tank fill with drain valve
prompts.text: A storage tank has an inlet pipe A that alone fills it in 5 hours, a second inlet pipe B that alone fills it in 8 hours, and a drain valve C that alone empties a full tank in 20 hours. Starting from an empty tank, all three are opened simultaneously. After 3 hours, valve C is closed while A and B keep running. Determine the total time, from the very start, until the tank is completely full. Show every step of your reasoning, including the combined rate calculations before and after the valve closes, and state the final answer as a decimal number of hours rounded to two places.

prompts.title: Conference scheduling combinatorics
prompts.text: A conference has 5 available keynote speakers and 8 available breakout speakers. The organizing committee needs to assign keynote speakers to open each of 3 conference days, where each day gets exactly one keynote speaker, no speaker repeats across days, and the order (which day each speaker gets) matters. Separately, the committee must also choose 4 of the 8 breakout speakers to fill an unordered shared 'unconference' time slot, where the order of selection does not matter. Calculate the total number of distinct overall schedules (keynote assignment combined with breakout selection), showing the permutation and combination formulas you used and the arithmetic that produces the final integer.

prompts.title: Flaky test draw probability
prompts.text: A QA lead has a pool of 15 test cases, 6 of which are known to be flaky and 9 of which are stable. She selects 4 test cases uniformly at random without replacement to run in a smoke-test suite. Compute the exact probability that precisely 2 of the 4 selected test cases are from the flaky set. Show the combinatorial setup using combinations, simplify the fraction as far as possible, and also give the result as a decimal rounded to four places.

prompts.title: Monthly compounding threshold
prompts.text: An engineer deposits $12,000 into a savings account that compounds monthly at a nominal annual interest rate of 6%. Determine the smallest whole number of months after which the account balance first exceeds $15,000. Show the compound interest formula you use, isolate the exponent using logarithms, and state the final integer number of months along with the actual balance at that month, rounded to the nearest cent.

prompts.title: Triangle area and largest angle
prompts.text: A triangular plot of land has side lengths of 7 meters, 8 meters, and 9 meters. First compute the triangle's area using Heron's formula, showing the semi-perimeter calculation and simplifying the square root as far as possible. Then compute the measure of the largest interior angle (the one opposite the longest side) using the Law of Cosines, showing the substitution and giving the angle in degrees rounded to one decimal place.

prompts.title: Acid mixture linear system
prompts.text: A chemistry lab needs to prepare 14 liters of a 40%-acid solution by mixing some amount of a 25%-acid solution with some amount of a 60%-acid solution. Set up a system of two linear equations in two unknowns representing total volume and total acid content, solve the system algebraically (show the substitution or elimination steps), and state exactly how many liters of each source solution are required.

prompts.title: Cyclists meeting with head start
prompts.text: Two cyclists start 63 miles apart and ride toward each other along the same straight road. The first cyclist rides at a constant 14 mph and departs first; the second cyclist rides at a constant 21 mph but departs 15 minutes after the first. Determine, measured from the moment the first cyclist departed, how long it takes until they meet. Show your work for the distance the first cyclist covers alone during the head-start period, the combined closing speed once both are riding, and the final total elapsed time expressed in hours and minutes.

prompts.title: Password type arrangement count
prompts.text: A security policy requires passwords to be exactly 8 characters long, composed of exactly 2 uppercase letters, exactly 2 digits, and exactly 4 lowercase letters, arranged in some order, with the additional constraint that the two digits may never be adjacent to each other. Treating each character only by its type (U, U, D, D, L, L, L, L) rather than its specific value, count how many distinct type-sequences of length 8 satisfy the no-adjacent-digits constraint. Show the total unrestricted arrangement count using the multinomial coefficient, then subtract the arrangements where the two digits are adjacent using the block/gluing method, and give the final integer.

prompts.title: Flaky test binomial probability
prompts.text: An integration test fails independently with probability 0.15 on each run, regardless of prior runs. If the test suite is executed 6 independent times, calculate the probability that it fails at least twice out of the 6 runs. Show the binomial probability mass function you use for exactly 0 failures and exactly 1 failure, compute both values, and subtract their sum from 1 to obtain the final probability, rounded to four decimal places.

prompts.title: Comparing two investments
prompts.text: An investor is comparing two options for a $10,000 deposit held for exactly 6 years. Option X compounds annually at a nominal rate of 5%. Option Y compounds monthly at a nominal annual rate of 4.8%. Compute the final balance for each option separately, showing the compound interest formula and the exponent used in each case, then state which option yields more money at the end of 6 years and by how much, rounded to the nearest cent.

prompts.title: Grain silo volume and fill time
prompts.text: A grain silo is shaped as a vertical cylinder of radius 3 meters and height 10 meters, topped with a cone of the same radius and a height of 4 meters. Compute the total volume of the silo by summing the cylinder's volume and the cone's volume, showing both formulas and leaving intermediate results in terms of pi before giving a final numeric value in cubic meters (use pi = 3.14159). Then, if grain is poured in at a constant rate of 2 cubic meters per minute starting from empty, calculate how many minutes it takes to completely fill the silo, rounded to one decimal place.

prompts.title: Server routing steady state
prompts.text: Requests to a two-region server cluster switch between Region A and Region B each hour according to a Markov transition matrix: from Region A, 90% of requests stay in A and 10% move to B; from Region B, 30% move to A and 70% stay in B. Find the steady-state distribution (piA, piB) such that the distribution no longer changes when multiplied by the transition matrix, and such that piA + piB = 1. Show the two balance equations you derive from the matrix, solve them algebraically, and state the final steady-state proportions as exact fractions and as decimals.

prompts.title: Warehouse crew shift output
prompts.text: A warehouse crew of 6 workers, all packing at the same constant individual rate, can together pack 900 boxes over a 5-hour shift. After exactly 2 hours into the shift, 2 of the 6 workers are reassigned to another task, leaving only 4 workers for the remaining 3 hours, all still working at the same per-worker rate as before. Determine the per-worker hourly packing rate first, then compute how many boxes are packed in the first 2 hours, how many are packed in the final 3 hours, and finally the total number of boxes packed by the end of the full 5-hour shift.

prompts.title: Full house card odds
prompts.text: From a standard 52-card deck, a 5-card hand is dealt at random. Calculate the exact probability that the hand contains exactly 3 kings and exactly 2 queens. Show the combination counts for choosing 3 of the 4 kings and 2 of the 4 queens, the combination count for the total number of possible 5-card hands from 52 cards, and simplify the final probability as a reduced fraction and as a decimal in scientific notation.

prompts.title: Hexagonal helipad measurements
prompts.text: A helipad is built in the shape of a regular hexagon with a side length of 12 meters. First compute the total area of the hexagonal pad, showing the standard formula for a regular hexagon's area in terms of its side length and simplifying any radicals as far as possible. Then compute the apothem (the radius of the largest circle that can be inscribed within the hexagon), showing the relationship between the apothem and the side length for a regular hexagon. Give both final answers, the area in square meters and the apothem in meters, rounded to two decimal places where applicable.

prompts.title: Running revenue per customer
prompts.text:
You are given the following schema for an e-commerce platform:

customers(customer_id INT PK, signup_date DATE, region VARCHAR, plan_tier VARCHAR)
orders(order_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL)
order_items(order_item_id INT PK, order_id INT FK, product_id INT FK, quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL)
products(product_id INT PK, product_name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR)

Write a single SQL query that, for every customer with at least one order with status = 'completed', lists each completed order's order_date and total_amount alongside a running (cumulative) total of that customer's spend ordered chronologically, using a window function rather than a correlated subquery or self-join. Also include a column showing each order's rank in that customer's order history by date. Return columns: customer_id, order_date, total_amount, running_total, order_rank. Explain briefly which window function clauses you used and why.

prompts.title: Overdue invoice detection query
prompts.text:
Here is a SaaS billing schema:

accounts(account_id INT PK, company_name VARCHAR, created_at DATE, status VARCHAR)
subscriptions(subscription_id INT PK, account_id INT FK, plan_name VARCHAR, mrr DECIMAL, started_at DATE, cancelled_at DATE NULL)
invoices(invoice_id INT PK, account_id INT FK, invoice_date DATE, due_date DATE, amount DECIMAL, paid_at DATE NULL)

Write a SQL query using a correlated subquery (not a window function) that returns every account whose most recent invoice (by invoice_date) is unpaid as of today (paid_at IS NULL) and is also past its due_date. For each such account, return account_id, company_name, the invoice_id and due_date of that specific most-recent invoice, and the number of days it is overdue. The correlated subquery must identify 'most recent invoice per account' by comparing invoice_date against all other invoices for the same account_id.

prompts.title: Device uptime gaps and islands
prompts.text:
Given this IoT fleet schema:

devices(device_id INT PK, device_name VARCHAR, site_id INT FK, installed_at DATE)
sites(site_id INT PK, site_name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
status_pings(ping_id INT PK, device_id INT FK, ping_time TIMESTAMP, status VARCHAR CHECK (status IN ('online','offline')))

Each device sends a status ping every 5 minutes. Write a gaps-and-islands SQL query that, for a given device_id, groups consecutive pings with the same status into contiguous 'episodes', and returns one row per episode with columns: device_id, status, episode_start (first ping_time in the episode), episode_end (last ping_time in the episode), and episode_duration_minutes. Use the standard technique of subtracting a row_number() computed within each status partition from a row_number() computed overall (or an equivalent approach) to identify the island groupings, and explain in one sentence why that subtraction trick produces a constant value within each island.

prompts.title: Streaming cohort retention query
prompts.text:
Consider this video streaming schema:

users(user_id INT PK, signup_date DATE, country VARCHAR)
subscriptions(subscription_id INT PK, user_id INT FK, plan VARCHAR, started_at DATE, cancelled_at DATE NULL)
watch_sessions(session_id INT PK, user_id INT FK, watched_at TIMESTAMP, title_id INT FK, minutes_watched INT)
titles(title_id INT PK, title_name VARCHAR, genre VARCHAR)

Write a SQL query that builds a monthly cohort retention table: group users into cohorts by the calendar month of their signup_date, then for each cohort, for each subsequent calendar month (month 0 through month 5 relative to signup month), compute the percentage of that cohort's users who had at least one watch_sessions row in that relative month. Return columns: cohort_month, months_since_signup, active_users, cohort_size, retention_rate. Show how you compute 'months since signup' as an integer difference between two calendar months.

prompts.title: Warehouse SKU running balance
prompts.text:
The following inventory schema describes a warehouse:

warehouses(warehouse_id INT PK, warehouse_name VARCHAR, region VARCHAR)
skus(sku_id INT PK, sku_code VARCHAR, description VARCHAR)
inventory_movements(movement_id INT PK, warehouse_id INT FK, sku_id INT FK, movement_time TIMESTAMP, movement_type VARCHAR CHECK (movement_type IN ('receipt','shipment','adjustment')), quantity_delta INT)

Note that quantity_delta is positive for receipts and positive adjustments, and negative for shipments and negative adjustments. Write a SQL query that, for a single given sku_id across a single given warehouse_id, lists every movement in chronological order along with a running on-hand quantity balance computed as a window function over quantity_delta, and flags with a boolean column 'went_negative' any row where the running balance dropped below zero, which would indicate a data integrity problem since physical stock cannot be negative.

prompts.title: Unresolved support ticket anti-join
prompts.text:
Here is a customer support schema:

customers(customer_id INT PK, company_name VARCHAR, tier VARCHAR)
tickets(ticket_id INT PK, customer_id INT FK, opened_at TIMESTAMP, subject VARCHAR, severity VARCHAR)
ticket_events(event_id INT PK, ticket_id INT FK, event_time TIMESTAMP, event_type VARCHAR CHECK (event_type IN ('comment','status_change','escalation')), new_status VARCHAR NULL)
agents(agent_id INT PK, agent_name VARCHAR, team VARCHAR)

Write an anti-join SQL query (using NOT EXISTS or LEFT JOIN with a NULL check, not NOT IN) that finds every customer who has at least one open ticket (a ticket for which no ticket_events row has event_type = 'status_change' and new_status = 'resolved') and has had no 'comment' event logged on any of their tickets within the last 3 days. Return customer_id, company_name, tier, and the count of such stale open tickets, ordered by tier and then by count descending.

prompts.title: Top students per department
prompts.text:
Given this university schema:

students(student_id INT PK, full_name VARCHAR, department_id INT FK, enrollment_year INT)
departments(department_id INT PK, department_name VARCHAR)
courses(course_id INT PK, course_name VARCHAR, department_id INT FK, credits INT)
enrollments(enrollment_id INT PK, student_id INT FK, course_id INT FK, term VARCHAR, grade_points DECIMAL)

Write a SQL query using a window function (RANK or DENSE_RANK, partitioned appropriately) that computes each student's overall GPA as the credit-weighted average of grade_points across all their enrollments, then returns the top 3 students by GPA within each department. Handle ties explicitly by stating which rank function you chose and why, and return columns: department_name, student_full_name, gpa, department_rank.

prompts.title: Overdue library members query
prompts.text:
Consider this library schema:

members(member_id INT PK, full_name VARCHAR, branch_id INT FK, joined_date DATE)
branches(branch_id INT PK, branch_name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR)
books(book_id INT PK, title VARCHAR, author VARCHAR)
loans(loan_id INT PK, member_id INT FK, book_id INT FK, checked_out_at DATE, due_at DATE, returned_at DATE NULL)

Define a member's 'overdue rate' as the fraction of their completed loans (returned_at IS NOT NULL) where returned_at > due_at. Write a SQL query using a correlated subquery that returns every member whose personal overdue rate is strictly greater than the average overdue rate of all members at their own branch. Return member_id, full_name, branch_name, the member's own overdue rate, and the branch average overdue rate for comparison, with both rates rounded to 3 decimal places.

prompts.title: Longest gym check-in streak
prompts.text:
The following schema models a gym:

members(member_id INT PK, full_name VARCHAR, membership_type VARCHAR)
check_ins(check_in_id INT PK, member_id INT FK, check_in_date DATE)
classes(class_id INT PK, class_name VARCHAR, instructor VARCHAR)
class_attendance(attendance_id INT PK, member_id INT FK, class_id INT FK, attended_date DATE)

Assume a member checks in at most once per day. Write a gaps-and-islands SQL query that finds each member's single longest streak of consecutive calendar days with a check_ins row (no missed days within the streak). Use the technique of subtracting a sequential day number from the actual date to produce a constant 'island' grouping key for consecutive dates, then aggregate by that key to get streak lengths. prompts.text:
The Ruby method below fetches sales data, formats it into a report, and writes it to disk, all in a single method that mixes data access, formatting, and I/O concerns.

```ruby
def generate_monthly_report(month, year, output_path)
  connection = PG.connect(dbname: 'sales')
  result = connection.exec_params(
    'SELECT product_name, SUM(quantity) as qty, SUM(quantity * unit_price) as revenue FROM sales WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sold_at) = $1 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sold_at) = $2 GROUP BY product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC',
    [month, year]
  )
  lines = []
  lines << "Monthly Sales Report - #{month}/#{year}"
  lines << '=' * 40
  total_revenue = 0
  result.each do |row|
    lines << "#{row['product_name'].ljust(20)} qty=#{row['qty'].rjust(5)} revenue=$#{sprintf('%.2f', row['revenue'].to_f)}"
    total_revenue += row['revenue'].to_f
  end
  lines << '=' * 40
  lines << "Total Revenue: $#{sprintf('%.2f', total_revenue)}"
  File.open(output_path, 'w') { |f| f.write(lines.join("\n")) }
  connection.close
  return total_revenue
end
```

Refactor this into separate methods for data retrieval, report formatting, and file output, so each concern can be tested independently (for example, the formatting logic should be testable without a database or filesystem). The public method generate_monthly_report(month, year, output_path) must keep its exact signature and return value, and no new gems may be added.
